cases.title: Equifax Data Breach Settlement
cases.organizationOrEvent: Equifax 2017 data breach and 2019 FTC settlement
factsSupported: FTC alleged Equifax failed to take reasonable steps to secure its network before the 2017 breach.
The global settlement included the FTC, CFPB, and U.S. states and territories.
lessonsLearned: Known vulnerability management and basic security controls can become enterprise governance issues when sensitive data is exposed.
Security control failures can create consumer protection, legal, financial, and reputational consequences.
implementationRecommendations: Maintain risk-based vulnerability remediation with accountable owners and escalation thresholds.
Use segmentation, monitoring, and evidence-backed control validation for systems holding sensitive personal information.
limitations: Use the FTC complaint and orders for precise allegations and obligations; do not generalize the settlement to organizations outside applicable law.

cases.title: First American Cybersecurity Disclosure Controls
cases.organizationOrEvent: First American Financial Corporation SEC settlement
factsSupported: SEC found senior executives responsible for public statements were not apprised of information relevant to assessing a cybersecurity vulnerability and disclosure response.
The matter involved disclosure controls and procedures related to a vulnerability exposing sensitive customer information.
lessonsLearned: Executives cannot exercise defensible disclosure judgment when material security information fails to move through escalation channels.
Technical remediation and disclosure governance need connected evidence flows.
implementationRecommendations: Define cyber-to-executive escalation criteria and disclosure decision records.
Test that security findings reach legal, finance, disclosure, and executive decision owners when thresholds are met.
limitations: The case concerns SEC requirements applicable to issuers; use it as a governance example outside that scope, not as a universal legal rule.

cases.title: Pearson Cyber Breach Disclosure
factsSupported: SEC announced settled charges concerning statements and disclosures about a cyber intrusion affecting Pearson.
The action addressed how known incident facts were reflected in public disclosure.
lessonsLearned: Risk disclosures should not remain hypothetical after an organization has relevant incident facts.
Cybersecurity, legal, investor relations, and disclosure functions need synchronized evidence.
implementationRecommendations: Reconcile public risk language against current incident knowledge before filing or publication.
Maintain documented review of incident facts that may affect external disclosures.
limitations: Use the SEC order for exact findings and legal conclusions; do not imply the case creates duties for non-issuers.

cases.title: Blackbaud Ransomware Disclosure
factsSupported: SEC charged Blackbaud over misleading disclosures about a ransomware attack and associated data exposure.
The action addressed disclosure controls and the flow of information about the incident.
lessonsLearned: Incident communications must evolve as facts become known.
Disclosure control design should include mechanisms for technical teams to elevate new material facts.
implementationRecommendations: Use incident fact registers with named disclosure owners and update triggers.
Require cross-functional review when ransomware investigations change the understood scope of exposed data.
limitations: Exact findings and obligations should be taken from the SEC order; issuer-specific requirements should not be generalized as universal law.

cases.title: Anthem HIPAA Cyberattack Settlement
cases.sourceAuthority: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office for Civil Rights
factsSupported: Anthem agreed to a $16 million OCR settlement and corrective action after cyberattacks exposed electronic protected health information.
The matter was handled under the HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules.
lessonsLearned: High-value regulated data requires sustained risk analysis, access safeguards, and monitoring rather than point-in-time compliance.
Corrective action can extend beyond incident containment into governance and program improvements.
implementationRecommendations: Maintain current security risk analysis and documented remediation for systems processing regulated health information.
Connect identity, access, logging, incident response, and executive oversight evidence.
limitations: HIPAA applicability depends on entity and data status; do not apply the settlement as a rule for organizations outside HIPAA scope.

cases.title: Penn State Cybersecurity Contract Settlement
cases.organizationOrEvent: Pennsylvania State University False Claims Act cybersecurity settlement
factsSupported: Penn State agreed to pay $1.25 million to resolve allegations concerning cybersecurity requirements in DoD and NASA contracts or subcontracts.
The allegations included failures involving required controls, plans of action, and reported cybersecurity posture.
lessonsLearned: Contractual cybersecurity representations need evidence that matches actual implementation status.
Plans of action and assessment scores are governance records, not administrative paperwork.
implementationRecommendations: Tie contract requirements to control evidence, remediation owners, dates, and representations made externally.
Require review of cybersecurity attestations and scores before submission to government systems or contracting parties.
limitations: The settlement resolved allegations without establishing universal liability; applicability depends on contract terms and governing law.

cases.title: Rite Aid Facial Recognition Enforcement
cases.organizationOrEvent: Rite Aid facial recognition FTC matter
factsSupported: FTC alleged Rite Aid failed to implement reasonable procedures and safeguards in its use of facial recognition technology.
The matter addressed testing, risk mitigation, consumer notice, data practices, and executive oversight.
lessonsLearned: AI deployment risk includes error rates, disparate impacts, operational misuse, and governance failures, not only model accuracy.
High-impact automated systems need predeployment testing, monitoring, escalation, and accountable human oversight.
implementationRecommendations: Require documented AI use-case approval, accuracy and harm testing, monitoring thresholds, human review, and retirement criteria.
Maintain auditable policies for biometric data collection, retention, access, vendor oversight, and consumer notice where applicable.
limitations: The matter is specific to its allegations and orders; legal requirements vary by jurisdiction and use case.

cases.title: Everalbum Facial Recognition Settlement
cases.organizationOrEvent: Everalbum Inc. FTC facial recognition settlement
factsSupported: FTC finalized a settlement involving allegations about facial recognition use and retention of users' photos and videos.
The order required express consent before certain facial recognition uses and addressed deletion obligations.
lessonsLearned: AI governance must account for the provenance and permitted use of training and operational data.
Privacy promises, consent states, retention practices, and model lifecycle decisions need technical enforcement.
implementationRecommendations: Bind AI data pipelines to consent, retention, deletion, and purpose-limitation controls.
Track whether models or derived artifacts require deletion when underlying data was collected or retained contrary to policy or commitment.
limitations: Use the FTC complaint and final order for exact requirements; other AI systems may involve different facts and laws.

cases.title: Uber Former CSO Data Breach Cover-Up Conviction
factsSupported: A federal jury convicted Uber's former chief security officer of obstruction of FTC proceedings and misprision of a felony in connection with conduct surrounding a 2016 breach.
The prosecution centered on actions taken after discovery of the breach while the FTC was examining Uber's data security practices.
lessonsLearned: Security leaders need clear ethical and legal escalation paths when incident facts intersect with regulators and disclosure obligations.
Incident containment cannot substitute for truthful governance, evidence preservation, and appropriate reporting.
implementationRecommendations: Establish legal and executive escalation for incidents involving regulatory inquiries, extortion, concealment risk, or disclosure questions.
Document incident decisions, preserve evidence, and separate legitimate vulnerability disclosure programs from breach-response obligations.
limitations: Criminal liability is fact-specific; this case should be used for ethical and governance lessons, not generalized legal conclusions.

cases.title: Centennial Peaks Workplace Violence Citation
cases.organizationOrEvent: UHS of Centennial Peaks workplace violence OSHA citation
factsSupported: OSHA cited Centennial Peaks Hospital after an inspection involving workplace violence hazards and documented employee injuries.
OSHA stated the employer failed to implement adequate measures to protect employees from workplace violence hazards.
lessonsLearned: Physical security risk needs documented hazard assessment, preventive controls, incident learning, and accountable remediation.
Repeated violence indicators should drive changes to staffing, procedures, environmental controls, reporting, and escalation.
implementationRecommendations: Maintain workplace violence risk assessments, incident trend analysis, preventive controls, training, and escalation criteria.
Integrate physical security and employee safety findings into enterprise risk and executive oversight.
limitations: The citation concerned a specific healthcare workplace and legal posture; apply lessons proportionately to the learner's environment.

cases.title: Abbott Pacemaker Cybersecurity Firmware Update
cases.organizationOrEvent: Abbott/St. Jude Medical pacemaker cybersecurity remediation
factsSupported: FDA records a 2017 firmware update intended to address cybersecurity vulnerabilities in Abbott, formerly St. Jude Medical, implantable cardiac pacemakers.
The remediation addressed identified vulnerabilities through device and supporting-system updates.
lessonsLearned: Connected product cybersecurity is a lifecycle responsibility that can require postmarket remediation.
Security decisions for safety-critical products must balance vulnerability reduction, operational continuity, and user or patient safety.
implementationRecommendations: Maintain coordinated vulnerability intake, risk assessment, update mechanisms, customer communications, and postmarket monitoring for connected products.
Include cybersecurity remediation capability and evidence requirements in product lifecycle governance.
limitations: Use current FDA guidance and device-specific records for regulatory obligations; this historical event is an instructional case, not current universal guidance.
